Name: Stardewiki
Author: Stopthatstings
Description:
Enough time for another harvest? Missing an ingredient? One more gift before the weekly limit? [b]Stardewiki brings the wiki and your current game information together in your pause menu[/b], so you can make a plan and get back to your farm.

Read about crops, villagers, gifts, recipes, items and places without switching windows. Open the [b]Wiki tab[/b] or press [b]F1[/b], type what you're looking for, and choose a result. You don't need to own an item or have discovered it first.

[b]Green Game cards[/b] use your loaded game data and current save. [b]Blue Wiki cards[/b] bring you the community's guides, tables and articles. Matching labels stay visible while you read, so you always know where the information comes from.

[size=5][b]Features[/b][/size]
[list]
[*][b]Browse the wiki in-game.[/b] Read articles, follow links, view images, and jump to sections like Gifts, Locations or Sell Prices.[/*]
[*][b]Make the most of today.[/b] Check weather, time, energy, health, luck, active buffs and skill XP in [b]My day[/b]. See birthday reminders, ready crops and machine output at a glance.[/*]
[*][b]Plan your next step.[/b] Check planting windows, missing recipe ingredients, villager relationships, animal care, building materials and more against your current game.[/*]
[*][b]Find the ingredients you already have.[/b] Cooking, crafting and building plans count your backpack, fridges and chests separately. See what's missing and which chest to check before gathering more.[/*]
[*][b]Make room for longer pages.[/b] Expand the reader for wide tables and images, then return to the menu without losing your place.[/*]
[*][b]Save your regular lookups.[/b] Keep favorites and recent pages handy. Articles and images you've already downloaded can be read offline.[/*]
[*][b]Start over without losing anything.[/b] The X beside search clears the current lookup and returns Home. Your favorites, history and saved pages stay put.[/*]
[*][b]Use the menu you already have.[/b] The Wiki tab works with the regular pause menu and with Better Game Menu.[/*]
[/list][size=5][b]Information from your game[/b][/size]

The [b]Game[/b] view goes beyond the usual reference page. It reads the state of your game and updates while the card is open.

[list]
[*][b]Skills and status:[/b] earned XP, progress to the next level, temporary skill bonuses, professions and recipe unlocks.[/*]
[*][b]Crops and orchards:[/b] planting outlook, first-harvest dates, seasonal regrowth windows, ready crop tiles and fruit-tree maturity. Crop estimates include Agriculturist and explain their watering and soil assumptions.[/*]
[*][b]Cooking and crafting:[/b] whether you've learned a recipe, ingredients across your backpack, fridges and chests, what's still missing and how many batches your materials cover. Chest locations help you find what to collect. Shared storage counts once, even when several chests open the same inventory.[/*]
[*][b]Villagers and gifts:[/b] friendship hearts, gifts today and this week, birthdays, current loaded positions and how a villager feels about the item you're holding.[/*]
[*][b]Farm and workshop:[/b] animal care meters, unpetted animals, building costs and materials, construction progress and the timers on your placed machines.[/*]
[*][b]Exploration and collections:[/b] current local conditions, equipment, mine progress, active quests, museum donations and other recorded collection counts. Shop cards show listed stock rules and supported player conditions.[/*]
[*][b]Fishing:[/b] your skill, location, season, time, weather, rod and bait, plus supported story requirements. See what's possible here and what still needs checking.[/*]
[/list]These cards use the data your game has loaded, including compatible data changes. Open a resource's Game card to see how much is in your backpack, fridges and chests. Counts refresh while you read, so moving ingredients updates the answer.

Stardewiki helps you plan with what you have. It doesn't move items, craft remotely, give gifts or change your progress. Having enough ingredients somewhere on the farm doesn't mean you can use them from where you're standing. Collect what you need, and let the game's crafting or cooking menu handle the rest. Uncertain requirements stay conditional; future loot and random outcomes stay a surprise.

[size=5][b]How to use[/b][/size]
Start with [b]My day[/b], or try [b]Can I plant Ancient Fruit today?[/b], [b]Can I craft a Sprinkler?[/b] or [b]How much XP for Farming?[/b] You can also look up [b]Abigail[/b], [b]Maki Roll[/b], [b]The Mines[/b] or any other wiki subject. Choose a result, switch between [b]Wiki[/b] and [b]Game[/b] where both are available, and use the section tabs to reach the part you need.

[b]F2[/b] looks up the item you're holding. The button in the reader's upper-right corner expands or restores it. [b]Escape[/b] leaves the search box first, returns an expanded reader to the menu next, and then closes the menu.

You can change shortcuts, switch offline mode on or off, and manage downloaded pages in [b]Settings[/b]. If another mod already uses F1, choose a different key there.

[size=5][b]Install[/b][/size]
[list=1]
[*]Install [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/2400]SMAPI[/url]. You'll need SMAPI [b]4.5.2+[/b] and Stardew Valley [b]1.6.15+[/b].[/*]
[*]Close the game and unzip Stardewiki into your [b]Mods[/b] folder. The folder should contain [b]Mods/Stardewiki/manifest.json[/b].[/*]
[*]Start the game through SMAPI. Look for the chicken-and-book Wiki tab at the right of your pause menu, or press [b]F1[/b].[/*]
[/list][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/32032]Better Game Menu[/url] is optional. If the tab can't be added, you can still open the reader with the Wiki button or shortcut.

[b]Updating:[/b] replace the files from the download, but keep your [b]config.json[/b] and [b]data/[/b] folder to preserve settings and saved references.

[b]Uninstalling:[/b] close the game and remove the Stardewiki folder. Keep a copy of [b]data/[/b] if you'd like to save your favorites and downloaded pages.

[size=5][b]Offline reading and privacy[/b][/size]
New wiki searches need an internet connection. Previously downloaded articles, images and the game's reference cards are available offline; the whole wiki isn't included in the download. Viewed pages are checked for updates after 24 hours by default, and the reader shows when you're using a saved copy. [b]Original[/b] opens the source article in your browser.

Online mode sends your searches and page/image requests to the official Stardew Valley Wiki. It doesn't send saves, player identifiers, credentials or diagnostic logs, and there are no analytics. Offline mode stops wiki requests. No account or paid API is needed, and Stardewiki doesn't download its own mod updates.

[size=5][b]Compatibility and known issues[/b][/size]
This is an early release for [b]Windows/Steam[/b], tested with [b]Stardew Valley 1.6.15[/b], [b]SMAPI 4.5.2[/b], and with and without [b]Better Game Menu 1.0.1[/b]. Other platforms, game versions and menu mods haven't been verified. Multiplayer and split-screen also still need testing.

The controls and wiki articles are in English; game reference names use your game's language. Some complex wiki layouts are simplified. Use [b]Original[/b] if you need to check the website's layout.

Game cards explain the limits of each answer. Crop forecasts assume daily watering, no fertilizer and no paddy-water bonus. Shop entries don't guarantee opening hours, available stock or final prices. Collection counts aren't a perfection score. Loaded characters and objects may change; future schedules, loot, random stock and routes aren't predicted. Custom conditions can require checking in the game or Wiki.

Storage counts include ordinary and big player chests, mini-fridges, home/cabin/island fridges and shared Junimo storage in loaded locations. Shipping bins, machine storage, other players' backpacks and virtual storage added by other mods aren't included. Unloaded locations or unusually large storage scans may leave more items to check; incomplete scans are labeled. Cooking uses only the fridges available to that kitchen. Workbenches and storage mods may have their own rules, so the card separates materials you own from materials you carry.

For fishing, casting position, water depth and other rules can still matter, so eligibility doesn't guarantee a catch. Crab-pot catches are shown separately; exact catch odds aren't included.

Found a problem? Please include your game and SMAPI versions, whether you use Better Game Menu, your UI scale, and what you were searching for or reading. A few steps to reproduce it will help. Please leave saves and personal information out of public reports.

AI was used to assist in the developemnt of this mod and creation of the cover illustration. Gameplay screenshots are unaltered; the mod has no in-game AI service.
